chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام): "Shall I present to you my religion by which I worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" He said: "Bring it forth."

He said: So I said, "I bear witness that there is no god except Allah alone, having no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, and affirming what he brought from the presence of Allah; and that Ali was an Imam whose obedience Allah made obligatory; then after him al-Hasan was an Imam whose obedience Allah made obligatory; then after him al-Husayn was an Imam whose obedience Allah made obligatory; then after him Ali ibn al-Husayn was an Imam whose obedience Allah made obligatory, until the matter came to him."
Then I said, "It is you, may Allah have mercy upon you." He said: "This is the religion of Allah and the religion of His angels."

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I testify; a formal declaration of belief
key_terms.إِمَامًا: a divinely appointed leader whose authority is to be followed
key_terms.الْإِقْرَارُ: affirmation and acknowledgment of revealed truth
key_terms.دِينِيَ: my religion or creed that I hold and practice
key_terms.رَسُولُهُ: His Messenger, referring to the mission of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the testimony of tawhid, affirming that no deity is worthy of worship except Allah

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi teach about tawhid, prophethood, and the Imamate in Shia belief?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a concise creedal statement combining tawhid, the risalah of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, acceptance of what he brought from Allah, and belief in the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali and the succeeding Imams عليهم السلام up to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام. It shows that acknowledgment of divinely appointed Imamship and obedience to the Imams عليهم السلام is treated here as part of the religion of Allah.
